newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fed official urges Japan to keep easy credit - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Fed official urges Japan to keep easy credit - Jiji.

text.p: A high-ranking U.S. Federal Reserve Board official has stressed the need for Japan to maintain its low interest rate policy, partly in order to stabilise U.S. financial markets, Jiji news agency reported on Tuesday, quoting unnamed sources.
Jiji quoted the sources as saying that the Fed official made the remarks in a meeting with executives of major Japanese research institutions.
The official was also quoted as saying that even if Japan were to raise its official discount rate, it must guide short-term interest rates below the discount rate.

The official was quoted as saying that Japan is not in a situation where it can raise its interest rates considering that its economy is in the process of recovery and the country is carrying out fiscal reforms.

If interest rates in Japan were to be raised, the interest rate differential between Japan and the United States would shrink and this would lead to capital outflows from the United States to Japan, the official was quoted as saying.
Thus, an increase in Japanese interest rates could rattle the U.S. stock and bond markets, he was quoted as saying.
